title: Migrate existing tests to typed parts shape
description: Once the typed Component ADT (ppa-ysr) lands, all existing 'parts == List(...)' assertions in tests/Path.pkl must change. e.g. List('/', 'srv', 'app') becomes List(Anchor('/'), Normal('srv'), Normal('app')); List('..', 'state') becomes List(ParentDir(), Normal('state')). This is a sizable mechanical diff; dedicated task to keep the typed-components issue clean.
acceptance_criteria: All existing tests in tests/Path.pkl pass under the new typed shape; no behavior regressions. README examples that show parts also updated.

title: relativeTo with Python pathlib semantics
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §3.4, add Path.relativeTo(other: module, walkUp: Boolean = false): module. Semantics match Python pathlib.PurePath.relative_to. a.relativeTo(b) returns 'a expressed relative to b'; invariant b.join(a.relativeTo(b)) == a (under lexical equality, modulo .. resolution).

Lexical only — no CWD synthesis. Throws on:
- style mismatch (unix vs windows)
- anchor mismatch (one absolute, one relative; different drives; different UNC shares)
- non-descendant when walkUp=false
- unresolvable '..'-in-base (CPython gh-105002)

walkUp=true mirrors Python 3.12's relative_to(other, walk_up=True), permitting '..' segments in the result. The unresolvable-'..'-in-base case still throws even with walkUp=true.

Pkl does not support user-defined catchable typed errors, so callers either pre-validate via startsWith (ppa-xqz) or let the evaluator fail.
design: Walk typed parts of both inputs; common-prefix detection; walkUp=false requires a to be a descendant of b (else throw); walkUp=true emits '..' for each remaining component of b. Style/anchor checks first.
acceptance_criteria: All examples in v3 §3.4 pass; throw cases throw with stable messages; walkUp behaves correctly. Includes regression tests for JDK-8066943 and CPython gh-105002. Works on both Unix and Windows once Windows lands.

title: Component-wise startsWith
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §3.5, add Path.startsWith(prefix: module): Boolean that does component-wise (NOT string-prefix) ancestor matching. String-prefix '/foo'.startsWith('/foo') matches '/foobar' — exactly the Zip-Slip / path-confusion bug class. Component-wise rejects '/foobar'.startsWith('/foo') because Normal('foobar') != Normal('foo'). This is the public escape hatch users should reach for before relativeTo, and the building block for Zip-Slip-safe extraction.

Regression tests must include:
- Component-boundary: Path.unix('/srv/appfoo').startsWith(Path.unix('/srv/app')) == false (the load-bearing case for Zip-Slip safety; Rust #93586 territory on Windows).
- Trailing-slash invariance: Path.unix('/foo/bar/baz/').startsWith(Path.unix('/foo')) and Path.unix('/foo/bar/baz').startsWith(Path.unix('/foo/')) both behave per the equivalence-class policy in ppa-jog. This is Rust #148267 (Oct 2025): in Rust, strip_prefix unexpectedly strips the trailing slash from /foo/bar/baz/. Our behavior should be consistent regardless of whether either side has a trailing slash.
design: Walk both 'parts' lists, element-by-element comparison using typed Component equality. Anchors must match exactly. Style mismatch (unix vs windows) returns false. Empty 'this' starts with empty prefix only.
acceptance_criteria: Path.unix('/srv/appfoo').startsWith(Path.unix('/srv/app')) == false (component boundary); Path.unix('/srv/app/config').startsWith(Path.unix('/srv')) == true; Path.unix('/srv').startsWith(Path.unix('/srv/app')) == false; anchor mismatch returns false. Works on Windows once that lands.

title: Trailing-slash equivalence with display preservation
description: Per pkl-path-v3.md §3.2, paths that differ only in trailing slash should belong to the same equivalence class for equality but preserve the original form for toString(). Examples that must hold: Path.unix('/foo') == Path.unix('/foo/'); Path.unix('/foo/').toString() == '/foo/'; Path.unix('/foo').toString() == '/foo'. This matches Java NIO's policy.
design: 'fixed path: String' stays canonical (slash-stripped). Add 'hidden display: String' that preserves the input trailing slash (excluded from equality, used by toString()). The existing withTrailingSlash() function stays as the explicit 'always slash' accessor and is distinct from toString().
acceptance_criteria: Equivalence-class assertions pass; toString() preserves input form; withTrailingSlash() unchanged; root and '.' paths handle the corner cases sensibly without producing '//' or './'.

title: Replace List<String> parts with typed Component ADT
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §3.1, replace 'parts: List<String>' with a typed sum: Component = Anchor | Normal | ParentDir. The existing shape mixes anchor markers (literal '/'), regular segments, and dot-dot segments as plain strings; this generalizes poorly to Windows (where the anchor can be 'C:\\\\', '\\\\\\\\server\\\\share\\\\', or '\\\\') and makes component-wise operations like startsWith and relativeTo bug-prone. Every correct stdlib path implementation is internally a fold over a typed component iterator.

This is a BREAKING CHANGE to the existing parts shape. All tests/Path.pkl assertions on parts must migrate (tracked separately).
design: typealias Component = *Anchor | Normal | ParentDir; class Anchor { value: String }; class Normal { value: String }; class ParentDir {}. CurDir is omitted because '.' segments are stripped during normalization. parts.first being an Anchor is the way to detect absolute paths.
acceptance_criteria: parts: List<Component> exposed; parent(), parents(), join() all work in terms of typed components; new tests assert the component shape for representative inputs; existing test migrations land via a separate task.

title: Verify Pkl 'hidden' field is excluded from structural equality
description: The trailing-slash equivalence design in pkl-path-v3.md §3.2 relies on a 'hidden' display field that preserves the input's trailing slash for toString() but does NOT participate in structural equality (so Path.unix('/foo') == Path.unix('/foo/') still holds). Per the bd memory pkl-module-structural-equality-recursively-compares-all-fixe, only 'fixed' properties participate in equality — but this needs an explicit regression test before we depend on it. Quick spike: write a tiny module with a 'hidden' property that differs across two instances, assert ==, see what happens.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) a test confirms 'hidden' is excluded from equality and the §3.2 design proceeds as written, or (b) the test shows it participates and a fallback design is chosen (drop the equivalence-class promise; or switch to a different mechanism such as deriving display from path alone).

title: Unix path API v3 improvements
description: Land the Unix-side improvements designed in pkl-path-v3.md (typed component ADT, trailing-slash equivalence with display preservation, component-wise startsWith, withExtension, relativeTo with Python pathlib semantics, plus a fix for the existing POSIX 4.13 leading-// bug and explicit Zip-Slip documentation in README). Most of these are breaking changes to the v0.0.1 Unix API; bundling them into a single v0.1.0 cut keeps the migration burden in one step.
design: See ../pkl-path-v3.md §3 (Pkl-side changes) for the full rationale and per-feature design. Implementation order: (1) verify Pkl 'hidden' field equality semantics (blocks trailing-slash design), (2) introduce typed parts (breaking — affects every existing parts assertion), (3) trailing-slash equivalence + tests migration, (4) startsWith, withExtension, relativeTo on top of typed parts, (5) docs and the POSIX-4.13 fix.
acceptance_criteria: All Unix improvements from v3 §3 land with tests, README is updated (including the Zip-Slip safety section in bold), the typed parts shape is consistent across both Unix and (forward-compatible) Windows surfaces, and the v0 → v0.1 breaking changes are documented in CHANGELOG.

title: Implement Unix Path joining API
description: Implement lexical path composition for Unix paths. Joining a relative path appends segments while joining an absolute path replaces the base. Do not collapse . or .. during joins.
acceptance_criteria: Join behavior is tested for relative child paths, absolute replacement paths, empty components, trailing separators, ., and .. segments with no implicit normalization.
close_reason: Implemented join function with tests covering relative appends, absolute replacement, root base, current-directory identity, trailing separators, and preserved dot-dot segments.

title: Implement Unix Path inspection API
description: Add pathlib/std::path-style accessors for Unix paths: string rendering, parts, isAbsolute, isRelative, root or anchor, name, stem, suffix, suffixes, parent, and parents.
acceptance_criteria: Unix path inspection methods return predictable lexical results for absolute paths, relative paths, root, empty paths, hidden files, multi-suffix files, trailing separators, ., and .. segments.
close_reason: Implemented name, suffix, stem, suffixes properties and parent, parents functions on the Path module with pathlib-style semantics. Tests cover absolute, relative, root, empty, hidden file, multi-suffix, trailing separator, dot, and dot-dot cases (123 assertions).

title: Design Unix Path data model
description: Define the minimal Unix-only Path shape in Path.pkl: stored path string, absolute/relative state, root or anchor representation, and segment parsing that preserves empty, ., and .. semantics as needed.
acceptance_criteria: The data model is documented in code or README examples and can represent empty, relative, absolute, root, trailing-separator, ., and .. segment cases without resolution.

title: Unix path API MVP
description: Implement the first usable version of pkl-path for Unix-style paths only. Paths are pure configuration values, preserve written . and .. segments by default, and avoid local filesystem resolution.
design: Start with a single Unix path flavor. Store enough parsed structure to expose parts, root/anchor, filename, suffix/stem, parent, and join behavior while preserving the original semantic segments.
acceptance_criteria: Unix Path values can be constructed, inspected, joined, and rendered without automatic . or .. normalization; behavior is covered by tests and README examples.
close_reason: MVP delivered; all sub-tasks (data model, joining, inspection, tests/README) are closed. v3 design (../pkl-path-v3.md) adds further improvements tracked under a new epic.

title: Two-distribution packaging: pkl-path and pkl-path-windows
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §2 'Distribution: stub-and-real', publish two distributions from a single source repo:

1. pkl-path (Pkl-only): no reader, no JVM dependency. Path.windows() throws a setup-instruction error.
2. pkl-path-windows: bundles the Kotlin reader binary + a PklProject snippet that registers the pklpath URI scheme. Path.windows() delegates via read().

Both share the Path.pkl source; the windows() factory is templated (or conditional via a build flag) to embed either the throwing stub or the read() call.

Includes:
- Build pipeline producing both ZIPs
- Distinct package names and version numbers (or a pkl-path-windows that depends on pkl-path)
- PklProject configuration documenting the reader registration
acceptance_criteria: Both distributions published to GitHub releases with download URLs that work in PklProject dependency declarations. README documents which distribution to install for which use case. A user who only needs Unix paths can use pkl-path with no JVM and zero setup.

title: Kotlin reader: relativize and normalize on parsed components
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §4, implement the relativize and normalize operations in the Kotlin reader, operating on the typed component list produced by the parser sub-issues (ppa-70y, ppa-ut2). Once the parser produces components, both operations are small (~50 LOC each).

Behavior:
- relativize: Python pathlib semantics (matching the Pkl-side relativeTo in ppa-hbh). Throws on style/anchor mismatch, non-descendant when walkUp=false, unresolvable '..'-in-base.
- normalize: collapse repeated separators, strip extraneous '.' segments. Does NOT resolve '..' (purely lexical, matches Unix-side policy).
- All comparisons case-insensitive (Windows convention; v3 §4 decision).
acceptance_criteria: relativize matches the v3 §3.4 examples for windows() inputs; normalize matches v3 §3.1 / §6 corner-case expectations on the supported subset; case-insensitive comparison verified by tests like 'C:\Foo'.relativize('c:\Foo\bar') == '..'.

title: Kotlin reader: scaffolding for Pkl external reader wire protocol
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §2 and §4, build the Kotlin external reader executable that the Pkl evaluator spawns. The reader is a separate child process speaking Pkl's external-reader stdio wire protocol; it is NOT a JVM class auto-loaded into the evaluator. Implementer must read the current Pkl docs for the exact protocol shape and pin the Pkl minimum version in PklProject.

Scaffold deliverables:
- Kotlin project layout (Gradle recommended)
- Stdio loop implementing the external-reader handshake and request/response protocol
- URI dispatch (pklpath:windows/parse, pklpath:windows/relativize, pklpath:windows/normalize)
- JSON envelope: success {ok: ...} and error {error: {code, message}}
- Errors NEVER leave via non-zero exit (that surfaces as opaque reader-crash to users)
design: Kotlin + JVM (or Kotlin + GraalVM native-image — see ppa for native-image build). Use kotlinx.serialization or jackson for JSON. Wire-protocol layer is small (~100 LOC); parser/relativize live in separate sub-issues.
acceptance_criteria: Reader binary speaks the protocol; pkl eval against a test module with read('pklpath:windows/parse?value=foo') round-trips and decodes the JSON envelope. Errors are JSON, never crashes.

title: Pkl-side windows() factory and reader-call helpers
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §3.3 and §3.7, add Path.windows(value: String): module and the supporting Pkl-side machinery that delegates Windows operations to the external reader. Includes:

- 'style: \"unix\" | \"windows\"' discriminator on the module value.
- URI canonicalization helpers (sorted query params, UTF-8 percent-encoding).
- read('pklpath:windows/parse?value=...') wrapping with JSON envelope decoding.
- For the Pkl-only distribution: Path.windows() throws an evaluation error with a stable message instructing the user to install the windows-enabled distribution. No read() call is made — Pkl evaluator does not provide catch-and-rethrow for read failures.
- For the windows-enabled distribution: actually delegates to read().
design: Two distributions are toggled at build time (templated Pkl module). The stub form uses 'throw' directly; the real form uses 'read'. Both share the same public API. URI canonicalization is in a small Pkl helper that sorts key=value pairs and percent-encodes; from/to remain directional (never swapped).
acceptance_criteria: Path.windows('foo') works (or throws clearly) per the active distribution. parse, normalize, relativize, parts, parent, name, suffix, startsWith all dispatch correctly via the reader on the windows-enabled distribution.

title: README Zip-Slip safety statement (in bold)
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §9, the README must explicitly state that lexical normalization alone is NOT sufficient for Zip-Slip / path-confusion safety. Users will reach for pkl-path for security checks; we must document the honest answer (no by itself) and prescribe the right pattern (component-wise startsWith against a normalized base, with the additional caveat that symlinks defeat lexical normalization). State in bold in the README.

Cite as illustrative examples:
- CVE-2007-4559 (Python tarfile, 2007): the canonical 'syntactic path handling at the consumer site is not enough' bug — pure path manipulation in the tarfile extractor doesn't validate '..' against the destination base. Used to argue why callers must compose normalize + component-wise startsWith, not rely on lexical normalization alone.
- CVE-2025-3445 (mholt/archiver, April 2025): current example showing this bug class is still being shipped in 2025, not historical.
acceptance_criteria: README contains a clearly-marked Zip-Slip safety section with the honest 'no by itself' answer in bold, an example using startsWith against a normalized base, and the symlink caveat.

title: Fix POSIX 4.13 leading-// non-conformance
description: Path.unix uses replaceAll(Regex('/+'), '/') which collapses any run of slashes. POSIX 4.13 says a path beginning with two slashes is implementation-defined (Python pathlib preserves '//' as the root); only three or more leading slashes must collapse to one. Same bug class as CPython gh-92737. Pre-existing in v0.0.1, not introduced by v3 work.
design: Special-case the leading // run in the unix() factory. Either preserve '//' verbatim as the root (matches Python pathlib), or document divergence to Java NIO collapse-to-one. Likely we follow Java NIO and document — but make the choice deliberate, not accidental.
acceptance_criteria: Path.unix('//etc').path matches the documented choice (with rationale in code/README); Path.unix('///etc').path == '/etc'; tests cover both single-, double-, and triple-leading-slash inputs.

title: withExtension function
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §3.6, add Path.withExtension(ext: String): module that replaces the final suffix. Common API request for config-rewriting use cases. Argument may include leading '.' or not; both forms work. Empty ext removes the suffix.

Examples (from v3 §3.6):
- Path.unix('/srv/config.toml').withExtension('.pkl') → Path.unix('/srv/config.pkl')
- Path.unix('/srv/config.toml').withExtension('pkl')  → Path.unix('/srv/config.pkl') (leading dot inferred)
- Path.unix('/srv/config.toml').withExtension('')     → Path.unix('/srv/config')
- Path.unix('/srv/README').withExtension('.md')       → Path.unix('/srv/README.md')
- Path.unix('/srv/.bashrc').withExtension('.sh')      → throws (.bashrc has no suffix per existing semantics)
- Path.unix('/').withExtension('.x')                  → throws (no name to modify)
acceptance_criteria: All examples above pass as tests, including the throw cases. No silent surprises; throw cases throw with stable messages.

title: Cross-platform test corpus and Windows docs
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §7, build a JSON-driven test corpus for Windows path operations, sourced from CPython's test_posixpath.py + test_ntpath.py + test_pathlib.py, Go's path_test.go + path_windows_test.go, and OpenJDK's test/jdk/java/nio/file/Path/. Each row tagged with provenance.

Every CVE/bug enumerated in v3 §6 becomes a regression test on the supported subset. Explicit list:
- CVE-2022-29804 (Go Clean(.\c:) → c:): Path.windows(r".\c:") must NOT become absolute.
- CVE-2022-41722 (Go a/../c:/b → c:\b): same family; path-confusion via lexical normalization.
- CVE-2025-23084 (Node.js path.win32.normalize relative→absolute).
- CPython gh-100162 (os.path.normpath(r".\C:\x") → r"C:\x"): same shape as Go's CVE; Path.windows must not convert relative to absolute.
- CPython gh-92737 (POSIX // collapse). Covered by ppa-79t but include as a regression.
- CPython gh-99029 (PureWindowsPath drive-relative): drive-relative form is unsupported per v3 §5; the regression is that we return JSON 'unsupported', not silently corrupt.
- CPython gh-103593 (splitroot Global/GLOBALROOT/etc): device namespace is unsupported; regression is structured-error response.
- CPython gh-105002 (relative_to walk_up + ..-in-base). Cross-test with ppa-hbh.
- JDK-8066943 (Paths.get('..').relativize → '../x'). Cross-test with ppa-hbh.
- Go #10802 (filepath.Rel drive-letter case): relativize must treat 'C:' and 'c:' as the same drive (case-insensitive comparison per v3 §4).
- Rust #93586 (Path::new('C:').strip_prefix('C:') panics): Path.windows('C:') is drive-relative → unsupported error; startsWith on the unsupported case must not crash.
- Rust #148267 (strip_prefix strips trailing slash from /foo/bar/baz/): startsWith must be invariant under trailing-slash differences (per the equivalence-class policy in ppa-jog).
- Rust #100833 (UNC //tmp/foo misparsed as UNC \\tmp\foo): UNC requires server AND share components; \\tmp\ alone must return JSON 'invalid'. Covered by ppa-ut2.
- CVE-2025-3445 (mholt/archiver, April 2025): doc-level reference for Zip-Slip; tests live in ppa-195.

Plus: README documents the Windows support matrix (v3 §5), the case-insensitive comparison decision (v3 §4), the FFI-via-reader hack (v3 §2), the two-distribution setup, and explicitly notes that filesystem case-sensitivity is NOT modeled (dotnet/runtime#100102 territory — per-directory NTFS case-sensitive directories will compare equal under our case-insensitive rule).
acceptance_criteria: Test corpus exists with provenance tags; CVE regression tests pass on the supported subset; README has a Windows section that includes the support matrix, case-insensitive comparison decision, FFI hack acknowledgment, and a setup guide for the windows-enabled distribution.

title: Kotlin reader: UNC path parser
description: Per pkl-path-v3.md §5, UNC paths (\\server\share\path) are supported in the Kotlin reader. Verbatim UNC (\\?\UNC\server\share\...) is explicitly out of scope for now and must return a structured 'unsupported' JSON error. Anchor representation: parts.first is Anchor("\\\\server\\share\\"). UNC requires both server AND share components — \\server\ alone is invalid (Rust #100833 trap).
acceptance_criteria: \\server\share\path parses with anchor \\server\share\\; \\server\ alone returns JSON error code 'invalid' (incomplete UNC); verbatim UNC returns JSON error code 'unsupported'. Component-wise startsWith and relativeTo work across UNC paths sharing the same server and share.

title: Kotlin reader: parser for absolute disk, rooted, and pure relative Windows paths
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §3 and §5, Windows path parsing happens in a separate Kotlin reader process (not pure Pkl). This task covers the clean-room parser for the supported non-UNC forms: absolute disk (C:\Windows, C:/Windows), rooted-on-current-drive (\Windows), and pure relative (Windows, .\Windows, foo\bar). Drive-relative (C:foo), verbatim (\\?\...), verbatim disk, and device namespace (\\.\...) are explicitly out of scope and must return a structured 'unsupported' JSON error.

Clean-room: do NOT line-port OpenJDK's WindowsPathParser. OpenJDK is a reference for shape and naming only; the Kotlin code must be independently written. See v3 §2.
acceptance_criteria: Parser handles absolute disk, rooted, pure relative; emits typed component list with Anchor/Normal/ParentDir kinds matching v3 §3.1. Drive-relative, verbatim, verbatim disk, and device namespace forms return JSON {error: {code: 'unsupported'}}. Comparison is case-insensitive (drive letter and components alike, per v3 §4). Tests cover all supported forms and the unsupported-rejection cases.

title: Design explicit path flavor API
description: Define how callers choose Unix versus Windows path semantics without using host-native defaults. Decide constructor names, flavor fields, rendering behavior, and how mixed-flavor joins should behave.
acceptance_criteria: The API makes Unix, Windows, and UNC behavior explicit, documents mixed-flavor behavior, and does not infer behavior from the machine evaluating Pkl.
close_reason: Design completed in pkl-path-v3.md §3.3 (windows() factory + style discriminator). Implementation tracked as a new sub-issue under ppa-x4j.

title: Windows and UNC path support
description: Add Windows path support to pkl-path per the v3 design (see ../pkl-path-v3.md). Windows parsing and relativeTo are delegated to a Kotlin reader process invoked through Pkl's external resource reader API; this is an FFI-via-reader hack documented at length in v3 §2. Scope is bounded by the support matrix in v3 §5: absolute disk, rooted, pure relative, and UNC are supported; verbatim, drive-relative, device namespace, verbatim UNC, and reserved DOS names explicitly fail with structured errors.
design: Two distributions: pkl-path (Pkl-only, Path.windows() throws), and pkl-path-windows (bundles the Kotlin reader). Reader is a separate child process speaking Pkl's external-reader stdio protocol; it is NOT an in-process JVM class. Clean-room Kotlin parser (no OpenJDK port — license incompatibility per v3 §2). Case-insensitive comparison across all components on Windows. URI canonicalization is the caller's responsibility (sorted query params, UTF-8, percent-encoded). JSON envelope for all expected errors.
acceptance_criteria: Path.windows() supports the v3 §5 success-matrix forms with parse, normalize, relativeTo, parts, parent, name, suffix, and startsWith all working. Unsupported forms throw a stable evaluation error with code 'unsupported'. Reader works under GraalVM native-image Pkl distributions. Two distributions ship and are documented.

title: Add Unix Path tests and README examples
description: Create a tests directory with Pkl tests for the Unix-only API and add README examples showing construction, inspection, joining, and the no implicit normalization policy.
acceptance_criteria: Project tests exercise the Unix MVP behavior and README examples demonstrate the intended public API, including preservation of . and ...
close_reason: README now demonstrates inspection (name/stem/suffix/suffixes/parent/parents), joining, and the no-implicit-normalization policy. Test suite already exercises the Unix MVP behavior (16 facts, 123 assertions). Fixed an unclosed string literal in the trailing-separator example.

title: Reader native-image build for cold-start latency
description:
Per pkl-path-v3.md §2 'Reader packaging', prefer GraalVM native-image for the reader binary so cold-start latency does not penalize every pkl eval. JVM fat-JAR + launcher script is the fallback if the native-image build is too painful for the GraalVM Windows toolchain.

Goal: per-platform native binaries (linux-amd64, linux-arm64, macos-aarch64, windows-amd64) bundled with the pkl-path-windows distribution.
acceptance_criteria: Native-image binaries build for Linux and macOS at minimum (Windows preferred but optional if toolchain is fragile). Cold-start latency under ~100ms for typical pkl eval invocations. JVM fallback documented if native-image is dropped for a platform.

title: Optional host path resolution integrations
description: Investigate optional integrations for real host filesystem path resolution (resolving symlinks, absolute path against CWD, case-canonicalization against actual directory entries) — distinct from the Windows path parsing handled by ppa-x4j. The v3 plan keeps pkl-path purely lexical, including on the Windows side where the external reader does parsing only. Real filesystem resolution still requires evaluator-provided behavior (JVM/Go/Swift evaluator's resource readers, or a separate external reader). The core package should remain lexical and not assume the host OS of the Pkl evaluator.
design: Keep pkl-path lexical. Treat host filesystem resolution as an opt-in integration layer implemented by the embedding runtime or by an external reader executable. Avoid making path resolution depend on the machine evaluating Pkl.
acceptance_criteria: Document whether host filesystem resolution belongs outside the core library; identify supported extension routes such as embedded evaluator custom readers and external readers; propose an optional API shape such as a pathresolve: resource reader without changing the lexical path semantics.

value: Pkl module structural equality recursively compares all 'fixed' properties. A fixed property that returns a fresh module (or cycles back to itself) causes infinite recursion in equality checks, even though Pkl properties are otherwise lazy. Fix: expose recursive/self-referential accessors (e.g. parent, parents on a Path module) as 'function' members instead of 'fixed' properties — functions are not part of structural equality. Symptom: pkl test hangs forever on assertions like Path.unix('/foo').parent == Path.unix('/foo').
